headline: Half-Life ported to Mac OS 9, 28 years later
summary: A dedicated developer has successfully brought the iconic first-person shooter to PowerPC-based Macs, nearly three decades after its original planned release.
details: Twenty-eight years after its initial planned release, the legendary first-person shooter Half-Life has been successfully ported to PowerPC-based Macintosh computers running Mac OS 9.
The port was achieved by GitHub user doctashay, utilizing a fork of the Xash3D FWGS re-implementation of the GoldSrc engine. This allows the game to be played from start to finish.
This significant release includes multiplayer support and even offers downloads for the Half-Life expansions, Uplink, Blue Shift, and Opposing Force.

The port is compatible with G3 and G4 PowerPC machines running Mac OS 9.0 or later. However, performance can vary significantly based on the GPU, with systems having less than 8MB of VRAM potentially experiencing performance issues.
caption:
Half-Life, originally planned for Mac OS 9 in 1999, has finally been ported to the classic operating system 28 years later.

Twenty-eight years after its initial planned release, the legendary first-person shooter Half-Life has been successfully ported to PowerPC-based Macintosh computers running Mac OS 9.

The port was achieved by GitHub user doctashay, utilizing a fork of the Xash3D FWGS re-implementation of the GoldSrc engine. This allows the game to be played from start to finish.

This significant release includes multiplayer support and even offers downloads for the Half-Life expansions, Uplink, Blue Shift, and Opposing Force.

The port is compatible with G3 and G4 PowerPC machines running Mac OS 9.0 or later. However, performance can vary significantly based on the GPU, with systems having less than 8MB of VRAM potentially experiencing performance issues.

Source: Hacker News
